final_scenarios.name: Freelance consultant's weekly capture-to-completion loop
final_scenarios.audience: Solo independent consultants and freelancers juggling several client engagements plus their own admin and business-development work in one account.
final_scenarios.objective: Turn an undifferentiated stream of client requests, meeting notes, and self-generated admin into a scheduled, prioritized population of tasks that is worked from daily rather than merely remembered.
workflow: Capture every incoming request and follow-up into a single Inbox container in one action, with no required fields, during calls or between meetings.
Triage the Inbox daily: assign each captured task to a client container or Personal, add a due date where a deadline exists, set priority, and attach a label for context (onsite, phone, deep-work).
Decompose any task larger than one sitting into sub-tasks inside the parent task, so 'Draft Q3 report' becomes outline, data pull, review, and send.
Schedule the week in the Upcoming and Calendar views, placing fixed client commitments on their dates and pulling priority-flagged tasks forward into free slots.
Work from the Today view each morning, ordering tasks by due date and priority and checking items off as they are finished so the open population shrinks in real time.
Set recurring tasks for weekly invoicing, monthly expense submission, and quarterly tax reserve, and let each instance re-materialize when its cycle advances.
Review the week's unfinished tasks on Friday, rescheduling rather than abandoning them, and complete a short weekly planning pass for the next cycle.
acceptance: Every captured item appears immediately as an individual open task in the Inbox and can be opened, edited, moved, or completed on its own.
A task created as a sub-task appears nested under its parent and can be completed independently without closing the parent.
A due date or priority assigned in triage causes the task to appear in the corresponding Today, Upcoming, or Calendar view without further manual placement.
Completing a task removes it from open execution views while preserving its record, and a recurring task reappears with a new date when its cycle advances.
Filtering by label or container returns exactly the tasks carrying that label or belonging to that container.

checks.reason: The scenario instantiates all three jointly-held structures of the defining core. Task-as-unit-of-record and open→done: acceptance #1 (captured item appears as an individual open task that can be opened, edited, moved, completed) and #4 (completing removes from open views while preserving the record). Managed organization: workflow steps 2–3 assign client/Personal containers, labels and priority and decompose into sub-tasks, matching 'managed organization (containers, decomposition, classification)'. Execution views over the population: acceptance #3 and #5 (due/priority drives Today/Upcoming/Calendar; filtering by label/container) match 'execution views over the population' and 'the daily surface is computed from the population's attributes'. Recurrence: acceptance #4 matches 'Completing an occurrence of a recurring task generates the next one on the rule's schedule.'

User, goal and workflow materially overlap peer scn_3d2691ba3380442e971f1131f3ae7379 ('Personal Week Planner'). Same user: that peer's audience is '独立工作者、自由职业者或知识工作者' (independent worker/freelancer) managing professional and personal matters, essentially the scenario's 'Solo independent consultants and freelancers'. Same goal: capture scattered items into tasks, organize by container/label/priority/due date, then work from Today/Upcoming until done. Same workflow loop: peer steps '收件箱中快速录入' → '归入容器…打标签、设优先级…拆成若干子任务' → Today/Upcoming → mark complete → '周期结束…回顾未完成任务，重新安排'; the scenario mirrors this with Inbox capture → client/Personal container + label/priority → sub-tasks → Upcoming/Calendar → Today → complete → Friday review/reschedule. The scenario's additions either are mechanism inside the same loop (Calendar placement, triage detail) or duplicate the separate recurrence peer (scn_722423687c5e417185ac3963a57286a3 — recurring re-materialization), leaving no distinct user/goal center of gravity. Compared but distinct: scn_133dcc8698b946f7acf110aaecc37783 and scn_67279018432643158b706ee0b4f9abfe (team/shared-list collaboration with assignment and comments — the scenario is solo), scn_9738941d26b6488ea798faec18bbcc50 (student coursework audience) and scn_722423687c5e417185ac3963a57286a3 (recurrence-first routine audience).

The seven steps form a coherent, usable end-to-end loop matching the leaf's 'Capture → organize → work → complete → review': (1) one-action Inbox capture with no required fields; (2) daily triage into client/Personal containers with due date, priority, label; (3) decomposition into sub-tasks; (4) weekly scheduling in Upcoming/Calendar; (5) daily work from Today ordered by due date and priority; (6) recurring admin tasks that re-materialize; (7) Friday review that reschedules rather than abandons. Each step has a clear trigger and output, and the loop closes back into the next cycle.

The five acceptance criteria are observable and cover the flow: #1 capture produces an immediately visible, individually actionable open task in the Inbox; #2 sub-task nesting and independent completion of the sub-task with the parent remaining open; #3 a due date or priority set in triage deterministically places the task in Today/Upcoming/Calendar with no manual placement; #4 completion removes the task from open views while the record persists and a recurring instance reappears with a new date; #5 filtering by label or container returns exactly the matching set. These are checkable by inspecting view membership and record state rather than implementation internals.

Boundaries are reasonable and stay within the Type: a single solo account, containers including an Inbox plus client and Personal containers, sub-tasks, labels, priority, date-driven views, completion history and recurrence. No unsupported assumptions are introduced (no team membership, approvals, custom workflow states or progress rollup, which the leaf explicitly places outside this Type). The scenario is internally consistent: the objective ('worked from daily rather than merely remembered') maps to Today-view execution in steps 4–5, and the acceptance criteria reference the same Inbox, client/Personal containers and Today/Upcoming/Calendar views named in the workflow.

leaf_quotes: A **Task Management Application** is an application whose world is a population of **tasks** — individually addressable, completable records of discrete items of work — which the user organizes into managed structures (containers, sub-tasks, labels, priorities) and works from through execution views (today/upcoming, calendar, board, filters) that the tasks' own attributes drive.
- task as the unit of record, open → done
- managed organization (containers, decomposition, classification)
- execution views over the population
Completing an occurrence of a recurring task generates the next one on the rule's schedule.

**Completion is the engine.** Everything the application reports — progress, streaks, overdue counts — derives from completion acts and due dates; no one approves, routes, or transitions the record through states.

final_scenarios.name: Small team shared list for delegation and follow-through
final_scenarios.audience: Leads and members of small teams (5-15 people) who need a shared place to hand off tasks and see what has been completed, without adopting a heavy workflow tool.
final_scenarios.objective: Coordinate a small group's work through shared containers where tasks are assigned to members and completion is visible to everyone, keeping every record in the simple open-or-done state.
workflow: Create one shared container per active workstream or client and add the whole team as members of that container.
Have members add tasks directly to the shared container, and have the lead add tasks and assign each one to a named member.
When delegating a large item, break it into sub-tasks and assign each sub-task to the right member, keeping the parent as the overall item.
Use priority and due dates to signal what matters this week, and attach labels such as blocked, waiting-on-client, or review to make status legible from attributes rather than from separate states.
Discuss specifics by commenting on the task itself so the conversation stays attached to the work item instead of scattering across chat.
Members work from a personal Today view that surfaces the tasks assigned to them alongside their private tasks in a clearly separated space.
The group scans the shared container's open and completed tasks at the end of the week to see what moved and what did not.
acceptance: A task assigned to a member appears in that member's assigned-task view while remaining visible in the shared container to all members.
A comment added to a task is visible to every member of its container and stays attached when the task is reassigned.
When a member completes an assigned task, its completion is observable to the other container members without any additional reporting action.
Sub-tasks can be completed and assigned independently of the parent task, and the parent remains open until it is completed directly.
A member's personal tasks never appear in a shared container unless the member deliberately moves or shares them.

checks.reason: The scenario targets the leaf's exact defining core: it keeps records in the two-state grammar ('keeping every record in the simple open-or-done state' against the leaf's 'A task is open or done.'), organizes 'shared containers' with sub-tasks/priority/labels, and works from an execution view ('personal Today view'). It matches the leaf's second user directly — 'Small groups and teams are the second user: shared lists or shared projects where members add tasks, assign them to each other, comment, and watch completion happen.' — and stays inside the leaf's collaboration boundary ('assignment selects an owner inside that circle'), explicitly avoiding workflow states, approval chains, or role machinery.

Material overlap with scn_133dcc8698b946f7acf110aaecc37783: same user (small team/family/interest group needing shared day-to-day cooperation vs. leads/members of 5-15 person teams), same goal (shared list where members add tasks, assign each other, comment, and see completion under a unified two-state status), and same workflow arc (create shared list → invite members → add and assign tasks → comment on the task → complete with status visible to all). The scenario's acceptance criteria 1-3 (assigned task appears in assignee's view while staying in the shared container; comments visible to every member; completion observable to other members) restate that peer's criteria almost verbatim. The other peers were compared and are distinct: scn_374d3e68906d4e0f94cbce2df195d5d6 (solo freelancer capture-to-completion), scn_3d2691ba3380442e971f1131f3ae7379 (personal week planner), scn_722423687c5e417185ac3963a57286a3 (recurring routine reset), and scn_9738941d26b6488ea798faec18bbcc50 (student term planning) are all single-actor scenarios with different audiences, objectives, and workflows.

The seven steps form a coherent end-to-end loop consistent with the leaf's canonical capture→organize→work→complete→review: create one shared container per workstream/client and add members; members and lead add tasks with assignment; decompose large items into assigned sub-tasks; signal urgency with priority/due dates and legible status via labels; comment on the task so discussion stays attached; work from a personal Today view separating assigned and private tasks; scan the container's open/completed tasks weekly. Each step has a clear actor and predecessor, and the whole is usable as described without missing transitions.

The five acceptance criteria are observable and cover the workflow's critical claims: assigned task appears in the member's assigned-task view while remaining visible in the shared container to all; a comment is visible to every container member and survives reassignment; completion of an assigned task is observable to other members without a separate reporting action; sub-tasks complete/assign independently while the parent stays open until completed directly; personal tasks never surface in a shared container unless deliberately moved or shared. Each corresponds to a concrete action the described workflow performs (assignment, commenting/reassignment, completion, decomposition, personal/shared separation), so they are evaluable without implementation detail.

Boundaries are reasonable and internally consistent: the audience is bounded to small teams of 5-15, the two-state grammar is repeatedly preserved ('rather than from separate states'), and no unsupported machinery (approvals, workflow states, progress rollup on containers, org roles) is assumed. The personal-vs-shared separation step is backed by the leaf's common/optional variant 'separated personal vs team workspaces in one account', and the sub-task/parent-open rule is a legitimate choice within the leaf's note that sub-task cascade rules vary. Remaining choices (specific labels, container count, review cadence) are usage detail, not unsupported assumptions.

leaf_quotes: A task is open or done.
**Small groups and teams** are the second user: shared lists or shared projects where members add tasks, **assign** them to each other, comment, and watch completion happen.

Sharing happens at the container level: members of a shared list/project can edit its tasks, and assignment selects an owner inside that circle. Personal containers remain private unless deliberately shared.

final_scenarios.name: Student's term planning across coursework and personal life
final_scenarios.audience: University and graduate students who must balance assignment deadlines, exam preparation, recurring study habits, and personal errands in one account.
final_scenarios.objective: Make a term's worth of coursework and personal commitments workable week to week by scheduling deadlines, decomposing large assignments, and building recurring study cycles that re-materialize automatically.
workflow: At the start of term, create a container per course and capture every syllabus deadline as a task with its due date.
Label tasks by type (reading, problem set, paper, exam, personal) and set priority so the heaviest work is identifiable before it becomes urgent.
Break each major assignment into sub-tasks with earlier internal due dates so the work starts well before the deadline.
Plan the study week from the Upcoming view, placing study blocks against upcoming deadlines and using a board or filter over labels to see the workload per course.
Work a daily Today view that mixes academic tasks and personal errands in one ordered list, completing items as they are finished.
Create recurring tasks for weekly lectures review, problem-set practice, and gym or habit routines, and rely on them to reappear each cycle.
Before each exam, filter to that course's label and work only from the filtered set until all listed tasks are done or rescheduled.
acceptance: Tasks entered with a syllabus due date land on the correct date in the Calendar and Upcoming views without manual rescheduling.
A parent assignment stays open while its sub-tasks are completed one by one, and completing all sub-tasks does not by itself mark the assignment done.
A recurring study task appears again on its next scheduled date after being completed, retaining its container, label, and priority.
Filtering by the course label returns exactly that course's tasks and excludes everything else.
Personal errands and academic tasks appear together in the Today view while remaining in their separate containers.

checks.reason: The scenario exercises exactly the leaf's defining core: the task as an open→done unit of record (acceptance #2, '#5 work a daily Today view ... completing items as they are finished'), managed organization (per-course containers, labels by type, priority, sub-task decomposition), and execution views over the population (Upcoming, Calendar, board/filter over labels, Today). It stays inside the two-state grammar with urgency derived from due dates/priority and uses recurrence re-materialization rather than staged workflow, matching the leaf's statement that completing a recurring occurrence generates the next one. No project-management rollup, issue-tracker triage states, or team role machinery is introduced.

Compared against all five peers. scn_133dcc8698b946f7acf110aaecc37783 and scn_67279018432643158b706ee0b4f9abfe are team/shared-list scenarios centered on invitation, assignment, and comment visibility — the reviewed scenario has no sharing, assignment, or comments. scn_722423687c5e417185ac3963a57286a3 is dedicated wholly to recurrence-rule semantics, whereas recurrence is one of seven steps here. The closest peers are scn_374d3e68906d4e0f94cbce2df195d5d6 (freelancer capture-to-completion) and scn_3d2691ba3380442e971f1131f3ae7379 (personal week planner): both share the canonical capture→organize→today→review loop, but the reviewed scenario differs in user (students), goal (term-scale course planning with exam prep and mixed academic/personal load), and concrete workflow (course containers from a syllabus, internal sub-task due dates, exam-time label filtering, recurring lecture/problem-set practice). Similarity here is the Type's shared canonical loop, not duplication.

The seven steps form a usable end-to-end loop: set up course containers and capture syllabus deadlines → classify by type/priority → decompose major assignments into dated sub-tasks → plan the week from Upcoming with board/label views → execute a mixed academic/personal Today list → run recurring study and habit cycles → filter to one course before an exam. Each step names a surface and a user action, and the sequence returns to execution and completion rather than stopping at setup, matching the leaf's 'Capture → organize → work → complete → review' loop.

All five acceptance criteria are externally observable and map onto the workflow: #1 date correctness in Calendar/Upcoming (steps 1 and 4), #2 parent stays open while sub-tasks complete (step 3), #3 recurrence reappears with container/label/priority retained (step 6), #4 course-label filter returns exactly that course's tasks (steps 4 and 7), #5 personal and academic tasks co-appear in Today while remaining in separate containers (step 5). None require inspecting implementation internals. Coverage of step 4's board view and of sub-task internal due dates driving Upcoming is only partial, which is a completeness suggestion rather than a blocker.

Boundaries are reasonable and internally consistent: one student account, coursework plus personal life, no sharing/team features, and no reliance on integrations, roles, or reporting machinery. Scope is term-bounded, which fits the audience and objective. The only tension is acceptance #2 pinning that completing all sub-tasks does not complete the parent, while the leaf says cascade rules vary by product — this is the scenario choosing one legitimate two-state variant as its observable contract, not an unsupported assumption.

leaf_quotes: A **Task Management Application** is an application whose world is a population of **tasks** — individually addressable, completable records of discrete items of work — which the user organizes into managed structures (containers, sub-tasks, labels, priorities) and works from through execution views (today/upcoming, calendar, board, filters) that the tasks' own attributes drive.
A task is open or done. Completing removes it from active views and writes it to history; un-completing brings it back (products typically require showing completed tasks first).
Completing an occurrence of a recurring task generates the next one on the rule's schedule.
The user works *from* these views, and completing a task updates the population everywhere.
Personal containers remain private unless deliberately shared.

与三个 peer 逐一比较：scn_4faa861048af4f8dac27dd44e531f25a（用户为独立研究者/撰稿人/研究生，按研究主题、章节或方法归类，动机是写作时找回来源）；scn_7756e0007f6a463a97316f3f49c15248（普通网络用户在“待购/家居改造/以后看看”等生活归类下暂存，尚未进入整理阶段，无“先保存后归类再由项目驱动浏览”的复访循环）；scn_8936303b326f4a43bee84d6e98f45f2d（学生按课程/学期累积，验收以“跨学期不清空”与课程分类为轴）。本场景用户为同时推进多个技术项目的个人开发者，目标是把技术文档、工具站点、参考链接按项目/技术栈归入私人索引，工作流以“切换到某个项目→打开对应分类浏览”为检索主轴，并以“项目结束后调整分类结构、移除非当前技术栈的过时条目”收尾，用户、目标与组织语义均与 peer 不同，属同一类型下的不同场景而非重复，无需修改。

六步构成可用的端到端闭环：一键保存（获取）→ 归入项目/技术栈分类（组织）→ 手工修正可辨认标题（可检索性）→ 切换项目按分类浏览（结构浏览返回）→ 按标题关键词或分类检索并打开原网址（检索与返回外部资源）→ 项目结束时重组/移删（维护）。与叶子 “Capture / Organize / Find and return / Maintain” 的流程骨架一致，且每步都可由个人开发者在真实场景中执行，分类自建也对应叶子 “Organization is user-controlled and always revisable”。题干未规定是否使用浏览器扩展或手动表单，属叶子明示的实现选择，不影响流程成立。

五条验收均可观察：验收 1 的“跨会话可再次访问”可用重启/新会话后条目仍存在来检验；验收 2 的分类创建、重命名、移动、删除可逐项操作并核对结果；验收 3 的“按关键词或分类检索可定位目标条目”给出明确返回判据；验收 4 的“打开导航指向其保存的外部网址”是可直接验证的跳转行为；验收 5 的边界排除项可通过确认不存在托管、发布或协作分享能力来核对。五条合起来覆盖了获取、组织、检索、返回、边界这一完整流程，未依赖主观判断。

边界清晰且内部一致：受众是个人开发者或小规模实践者，用量与“项目/技术栈”分类规模相符；验收第 5 条主动排除代码托管、资料发布和团队协作分享，与叶子 “**Private by default.** The library is personal” 不冲突（叶子中团队共享与公开发布本就是可选次要情境），属于合理的范围收缩而非矛盾。场景未断言市场规模、性能指标或具体实现方案，也未把叶子列为“成熟产品的标准配置”（扩展、自动元数据、快照、去重等）当作必需前提，无不受支持的假设。

leaf_quotes: The essential job is **save now, find later**.
**Reference record anchored to an address** — the central object is a record that points at a web resource via its URL, enriched with whatever metadata the product adds.
**Deliberate capture** — every record originates from a user decision to save (a click, a share, a pasted URL, an approved import). Nothing is logged automatically.
**Persistent, accumulating personal library** — records survive sessions and devices and pile up over time into a long-lived personal asset, often numbering thousands of items.

**User-controlled organization and retrieval** — the user structures the library in some form and can find records again by browsing that structure and/or by searching. The *form* of organization is an implementation choice, not part of the definition.

Retrieval is the loop the whole Type exists for. Results are the user's own records; the product finds things the user has already seen and chosen to keep — the inverse of a search engine, which finds things the user has never seen.
**Private by default.** The library is personal; visibility to others requires an explicit sharing act (a public link, a per-record flag, or an invited member).

retained_failures.reason: Review marked distinctness passed while listing materially overlapping scenario IDs; validator rejected contradiction. Clarified prompt and retried without regenerating drafts.
Model returned malformed final JSON (missing closing array bracket); original response retained and not counted as a valid report.

fixes: Provide byte-faithful leaf.md alongside full JSON input to avoid per-line read truncation; grant only exact document read paths.
Clarify related_scenario_ids denotes material overlap, not all compared peers.
operator_observations: The generation stage has only the leaf document, not existing scene context, so repeated production can duplicate earlier scenes; provide pinned existing scenarios before broader rollout.
Three task scenarios were generated in English despite the Chinese UI; output locale should be explicit in the generation input.
Review judgments are advisory and differ across attempts; do not treat model pass as human confirmation or market/runtime validation.
